beats.say: A penny gets you a library of records. And the bill arrives later.
Sign up and get twelve CDs for a cent.
Or pay full price for each CD you choose later.
Or join a club that ships a new CD every month.
The free-penny deal looks like a gift.
But members who ignored the deadline got a full-price album shipped - sounds generous.
But it forces a paid shipment.
The tiny clause auto-orders the next CD unless you say no, turning a penny into a bill.
That clause drove revenue to $1.4 billion in 1996.
When the model collapsed, sales fell to $17 million by 2014 and the parent filed bankruptcy in 2015.
Gym: free trial week, then mandatory $30 class each visit.
Café: buy one coffee for $1, then auto-add $5 pastry each day.
Streaming app: $0.99 first month, then $12 monthly subscription - the recurring charge feels like the real deal.
Watch the fine print for automatic charges. Follow for more.
